label: Error Doctor: what happens to each error, and its limits

params.name: rules

default.pattern: (?i)failed to fetch|networkerror|load failed|aborterror|the user aborted|resizeobserver loop
default.say: The browser lost its connection or closed a page part-way - nothing to fix.
A background job was left half-way by a restart; it was stopped cleanly so it can run again.
A paid service refused the key or ran out of credit. Open Key Management, check the key and top up, then try again.
The mail server refused to send. Open Projects & portal > Mail, check the sender and its password.
The server's disk is full. Ask your hosting to add space, or remove old backups and videos.
A fault in the code itself.

params.label: What happens to an error: the first row whose pattern (a regular expression over 'type: message @ where line') matches decides - who = auto (op fixes it here), claude (a Fix request to Claude), owner (only a person can: say tells what to do), ignore (counted only)

params.name: max_rows
params.label: Most different errors kept (the oldest goes)

params.name: report_rate
params.label: The rate (chip limits.rates) a browser may report screen errors at

params.name: fixed_status
params.label: The Reported issues status a fixed error is filed with

params.name: fix_project
params.label: The project a Fix request goes to (blank = the portal's own project of that name, else none)

params.name: fix_part
params.label: The module a Fix request is filed under

description_nl: 2026-10-20 owner: one Error module for every portal - errors caught, fixed where a generic op can, sent to Claude when it is code, told to the owner only when a person must act.
